description: Deontic constraint corpus for Tier 2. Each item is one engineering subject expressed four ways: the governing rule, its plausible negation, a paraphrase of the rule that preserves meaning while changing surface form, and a natural-language query an agent might issue when about to touch that subject. The negations are written as rules someone could genuinely have adopted, not strawmen, because a strawman negation would be easy to tell apart and would flatter the result.

items.rule: Never use an ORM in the billing module; every query there is hand-written SQL.
items.negation: Use the ORM in the billing module; every query there goes through the model layer.
items.paraphrase: The billing module must not depend on any object-relational mapper — write its SQL by hand.
items.query: Can I add SQLAlchemy models to the billing service?

items.rule: Route all database connections through PgBouncer rather than pooling in the application.
items.negation: Pool database connections in the application rather than routing them through PgBouncer.
items.paraphrase: Application processes must not maintain their own connection pools; PgBouncer sits in front of Postgres.
items.query: Should the worker open its own connection pool to Postgres?

items.rule: Migrations are forward-only; never write a down migration.
items.negation: Every migration must ship with a matching down migration so it can be rolled back.
items.paraphrase: Schema changes roll forward only — reversal scripts are not part of this project's migration story.
items.query: Do I need to add a rollback step to this migration?

items.rule: Rows are never hard-deleted; set deleted_at and filter in the query layer.
items.negation: Delete rows outright; do not carry a deleted_at column or filter for it.
items.paraphrase: Deletion is logical, not physical — records stay in the table with a deletion timestamp.
items.query: Can I just DELETE these expired records?

items.rule: Use UUIDv7 primary keys; never auto-incrementing integers.
items.negation: Use auto-incrementing integer primary keys; never UUIDs.
items.paraphrase: Every table's primary key is a time-ordered UUID rather than a sequence-backed integer.
items.query: What should the primary key type be on this new table?

items.rule: Store money as integer minor units; never as a floating-point value.
items.negation: Store money as a decimal floating-point value rather than as integer minor units.
items.paraphrase: Monetary amounts are persisted in cents as whole numbers — no floats anywhere in the money path.
items.query: Can this price field be a float?

items.rule: Persist all timestamps in UTC; never store a local time.
items.negation: Persist timestamps in the user's local timezone rather than converting to UTC.
items.paraphrase: Every stored instant is normalised to UTC before it reaches the database.
items.query: Should I store the user's timezone offset with this timestamp?

items.rule: Never write personally identifying information to application logs.
items.negation: Log personally identifying information so that support can trace individual users.
items.paraphrase: Log output must be free of names, emails and other identifying user data.
items.query: Can I log the customer's email address here to help debugging?

items.rule: Secrets are read from the secret manager at runtime; never from environment variables.
items.negation: Secrets are read from environment variables at runtime; never from a secret manager.
items.paraphrase: Credentials must be fetched from the managed secret store rather than injected into the process environment.
items.query: Where should this API token come from at runtime?

items.rule: Authenticate with server-side sessions; never with stateless JWTs.
items.negation: Authenticate with stateless JWTs; never with server-side sessions.
items.paraphrase: Auth state lives in a server-held session store, not in a self-contained signed token.
items.query: Should this new endpoint validate a JWT?

items.rule: CORS origins are enumerated explicitly; never use a wildcard origin.
items.negation: Allow a wildcard CORS origin rather than enumerating each permitted origin.
items.paraphrase: Only named origins may be permitted by the cross-origin policy — no catch-all.
items.query: Can I set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to * for this route?

items.rule: Never swallow an exception silently; every catch either handles or rethrows.
items.negation: Swallow expected exceptions silently rather than handling or rethrowing them.
items.paraphrase: An empty catch block is not permitted — errors are either dealt with or propagated.
items.query: Can I wrap this in a try/catch and ignore the error?

items.rule: Never retry a write automatically; surface the failure to the caller.
items.negation: Retry failed writes automatically rather than surfacing the failure to the caller.
items.paraphrase: Write paths must not have automatic retry logic — a failed write is reported upward.
items.query: Should I add exponential backoff retries around this insert?

items.rule: Consumers assume at-least-once delivery and must be idempotent.
items.negation: Consumers may assume exactly-once delivery and need not be idempotent.
items.paraphrase: Message handlers have to tolerate duplicates, because the queue can redeliver.
items.query: Can this handler assume it only sees each message once?

items.rule: Caches expire by TTL only; never invalidate on write events.
items.negation: Invalidate caches on write events rather than relying on TTL expiry.
items.paraphrase: Cache freshness is governed purely by time-to-live, not by publish-on-change hooks.
items.query: Should writing this record bust the cache entry?

items.rule: Rate limiting happens at the edge proxy; never inside application code.
items.negation: Rate limiting happens inside application code; never at the edge proxy.
items.paraphrase: Request throttling is the gateway's job — services themselves do not count requests.
items.query: Where do I add a rate limiter for this endpoint?

items.rule: Deferred work runs on queue workers; never on cron jobs.
items.negation: Deferred work runs on cron jobs; never on queue workers.
items.paraphrase: Scheduled processing is driven by the job queue rather than by timed crontab entries.
items.query: Can I add a nightly cron entry to process these records?

items.rule: Realtime updates use server-sent events; never WebSockets.
items.negation: Realtime updates use WebSockets; never server-sent events.
items.paraphrase: Push-to-client traffic goes over SSE, not over a bidirectional socket.
items.query: Should I open a WebSocket for these live updates?

items.rule: API versions are carried in the URL path; never in a request header.
items.negation: API versions are carried in a request header; never in the URL path.
items.paraphrase: The version identifier belongs in the route itself rather than in content negotiation.
items.query: How should this new endpoint expose its version?

items.rule: The public API is REST only; never add a GraphQL surface.
items.negation: The public API should expose GraphQL alongside its REST routes.
items.paraphrase: No GraphQL gateway belongs in this system — resource routes are the whole external interface.
items.query: Could we add a GraphQL endpoint for the mobile client?

items.rule: Clients upload directly to object storage with presigned URLs; files never pass through the API.
items.negation: Clients upload through the API, which then forwards files to object storage.
items.paraphrase: File bytes must not transit application servers — hand the client a presigned target instead.
items.query: Should the upload endpoint accept the file body and forward it to S3?

items.rule: Services communicate over the message bus; never by direct synchronous HTTP calls to each other.
items.negation: Services communicate by direct synchronous HTTP calls; never over the message bus.
items.paraphrase: Inter-service traffic is asynchronous and brokered — no service calls another's endpoint directly.
items.query: Can the orders service call the inventory service's REST API?

items.rule: The published package must have zero runtime dependencies.
items.negation: The published package may take runtime dependencies where they save implementation effort.
items.paraphrase: Nothing ships in the dependency tree of the released artifact — vendor or hand-roll instead.
items.query: Can I pull in a small npm package for YAML parsing?

items.rule: New dependencies require a recorded decision before they are added.
items.negation: New dependencies may be added freely without a recorded decision.
items.paraphrase: Adding a library is a reviewable choice that must be written down first.
items.query: Do I need approval before adding this library?

items.rule: Target Node 20 and above; never rely on APIs that require a newer runtime.
items.negation: Target the latest Node release and use its newest APIs freely.
items.paraphrase: The supported runtime floor is Node 20, so nothing newer may be depended upon.
items.query: Can I use this Node 24-only API here?

items.rule: Container images build from distroless bases; never from a full distribution image.
items.negation: Container images build from a full distribution base rather than a distroless one.
items.paraphrase: Runtime images must not carry a shell or package manager — build on a minimal base.
items.query: Can I switch this Dockerfile to the ubuntu base image?

items.rule: Workloads run on ECS; never introduce Kubernetes.
items.negation: Workloads run on Kubernetes; never on ECS.
items.paraphrase: Container scheduling stays on the managed ECS platform — no cluster of our own.
items.query: Should this new service get a Kubernetes deployment manifest?

items.rule: All infrastructure is provisioned through Terraform; never by console changes.
items.negation: Infrastructure may be provisioned by console changes rather than through Terraform.
items.paraphrase: Cloud resources come into existence through committed configuration, not through the web UI.
items.query: Can I just create this bucket in the AWS console?

items.rule: Terraform state lives in the remote backend; never commit state files.
items.negation: Terraform state files are committed to the repository rather than kept in a remote backend.
items.paraphrase: State is stored remotely and locked — it must not enter version control.
items.query: Should I check in the tfstate file?

items.rule: Database tests run against a real Postgres container; never against a mock.
items.negation: Database tests run against a mock; never against a real Postgres container.
items.paraphrase: Persistence tests exercise an actual database instance rather than a stubbed interface.
items.query: Can I mock the database in this test?

items.rule: Coverage is reported but never gated in CI.
items.negation: Coverage is gated in CI and builds fail below the threshold.
items.paraphrase: The pipeline publishes coverage numbers without failing the build on them.
items.query: Should I make CI fail if coverage drops?

items.rule: Never use snapshot tests for component output; assert on behaviour instead.
items.negation: Use snapshot tests for component output rather than asserting on behaviour.
items.paraphrase: Serialized-output comparisons are not an accepted testing technique here — test what it does.
items.query: Can I add a snapshot test for this component?

items.rule: A flaky test is deleted or fixed immediately; never marked as skipped.
items.negation: A flaky test may be marked as skipped until someone has time to fix it.
items.paraphrase: Intermittent tests do not get quarantined — repair them or remove them the same day.
items.query: Can I skip this intermittently failing test for now?

items.rule: Styling uses utility classes; never CSS-in-JS.
items.negation: Styling uses CSS-in-JS; never utility classes.
items.paraphrase: Components are styled through composable utility class names rather than runtime style objects.
items.query: Can I use styled-components for this new view?

items.rule: Server data is held in the query cache; never mirrored into a global store.
items.negation: Server data is mirrored into the global store rather than held in the query cache.
items.paraphrase: Remote state stays in the data-fetching layer and must not be copied into application-wide state.
items.query: Should I put this fetched data into the Redux store?

items.rule: The initial bundle stays under 200 KB gzipped; never ship a larger first load.
items.negation: The initial bundle size is not constrained; ship whatever the feature requires.
items.paraphrase: First-load JavaScript has a hard ceiling that new code must not push past.
items.query: Is there a size limit I need to respect for this new dependency?

items.rule: The mobile client is offline-first; every screen must render from local cache.
items.negation: The mobile client is network-first; screens may require a live connection to render.
items.paraphrase: Nothing in the app may depend on connectivity to display — local data backs every view.
items.query: Can this screen show a spinner until the network responds?

items.rule: Push notifications carry no payload data; the client fetches after waking.
items.negation: Push notifications carry their payload data so the client can render without fetching.
items.paraphrase: Notification messages are bare signals — content is retrieved once the app is awake.
items.query: Can I include the message body in the push payload?

items.rule: Analytics events are defined in the shared schema before use; never ad hoc.
items.negation: Analytics events may be emitted ad hoc without prior schema definition.
items.paraphrase: Every tracked event must exist in the central definition file before code emits it.
items.query: Can I fire a new tracking event from here?

items.rule: The CLI collects no telemetry of any kind.
items.negation: The CLI collects anonymous usage telemetry to guide development.
items.paraphrase: Nothing about a user's usage is reported back — the tool phones home never.
items.query: Could we add anonymous usage stats to the CLI?
